evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says: 'we received your request for an estimate for your upcoming move on October 14th which is Wednesday and I just need ten to fifteen minutes of your time so we can give you the estimate. Is this a good time to talk about the move?' — frames time but skips the dependable-quote promise and moves ahead without a clear wait.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after probing: 'Before I proceed, do you have any other concerns aside from the pricing?' comes before detailed logistics, but only gets a yes/no, not opened up into a genuine agenda discovery.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer says 'No' to concerns; no concerns raised = N/A.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No concerns raised; no reflection needed = N/A.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Covered: property type (apartment), floor/stories (5th floor, 3rd floor destination), number of rooms (1 bedroom worth of items from 3-bedroom unit), walking distances (50 ft + 10-15 ft current; 15 ft destination), furniture/special items (70-inch TV, marble table, dresser, rugs, bookcase, desk, chair, bedside table), access type (elevator vs. stairs). Full coverage.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Asked: 'if we're all moving a one bedroom apartment worth of items we normally see fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you think you would follow within that range?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full anchor: '$208 per hour for two movers... 2.5-hour minimum, prorated in 15-minute increments... estimate the move to be on the minimum... 2.5 to 3.5 hours... your estimate cost is between $520 [and] $728.' Personalized to the partial move and access challenges.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Both present: fee structure disclosed ($208/hour, no hidden fees listed explicitly: 'No credit card fees, no terrible fees, no assemble or reassemble fee, no transportation fees') and commitment framing (2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments).
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moves directly to 'if something comes up... you are free to reschedule' and 'would you like to be on the schedule for Wednesday October 14th?' with no fairness check.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No Two Promises section delivered, so no loop to close.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep jumps to 'Do you have any questions before I let you go?' — a throwaway close, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never explicitly asked. Rep says 'would you like to be on the schedule for Wednesday October 14th?' (a soft ask about scheduling), and customer volunteers 'yeah, you can go ahead and put me down for the fourteenth' — but the rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' directly.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Implied via deposit statement: 'we do not require any deposit. So if something comes up... you are free to reschedule' — no explicit rate-lock or no-deposit commitment phrased as promised.

top_strength: Jeline gathered comprehensive logistics details and delivered a clear, anchored, personalized estimate with full fee transparency and minimum-commitment framing in under 12 minutes.
coaching_note: Section 2's agenda question (asked after probing had begun) and the entire Section 5 (Two Promises) and Section 6 (final concerns check) were skipped or underdeveloped; prioritize asking 'What are your biggest concerns?' before probing logistics, deliver the On-Time Guarantee and Damage Coverage promises explicitly, and ask a genuine final-concerns check ('What's still concerning you?') before closing.
